nodes.description: In Glut1-deficient mice, low endothelial GLUT1 arrests postnatal cerebral angiogenesis and leaves a profoundly reduced brain microvasculature while barrier integrity is preserved. Pre-symptomatic AAV9-mediated GLUT1 repletion averts the vascular defect and the disease; late (adult) repletion does not. The 2020 consensus statement adopts impaired microvascular development as a complication of delayed treatment, but direct human vascular data are lacking, so this node is provisional and is the structural basis of an emerging, non-fuel mechanism.

nodes.description: Erythrocytes express the same GLUT1 transporter as the brain endothelium, so the haploinsufficient state is measurable outside the brain as reduced 3-O-methyl-D-glucose uptake (typically about half of control Vmax with an unchanged Km) and, with flow cytometry, as reduced surface GLUT1. Residual uptake tracks clinical severity. Certain pore-region alleles additionally render the mutant transporter leaky to cations, disturbing red-cell sodium, potassium and calcium and producing echinocytosis and hemolysis. This node is chiefly a diagnostic surrogate of the primary lesion; only the cation leak branch is itself pathogenic.

nodes.description: GLUT1 is the transporter responsible for facilitated glucose diffusion across the endothelial cells that form the blood-brain barrier, as well as glucose uptake into erythrocytes. Reduced GLUT1 activity impairs the rate at which glucose can be delivered from blood to brain, independent of blood glucose concentration.

evidence.reference_title: Glucose Transporter Type 1 Deficiency Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Glucose, the essential metabolic fuel for the brain, is transported into the brain exclusively by the protein glucose transporter type 1 (Glut1) across the endothelial cells forming the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Glut1DS results from the inability of Glut1 to transfer sufficient glucose across the BBB to meet the glucose demands of the brain.

nodes.description: Triheptanoin is an anaplerotic odd-chain (C7) medium-chain triglyceride that provides Krebs-cycle substrates and an alternative brain fuel independent of GLUT1. An open-label study reported marked reduction of non-epileptic paroxysmal manifestations and normalized brain bioenergetics, but a subsequent randomized placebo-controlled trial did not show a significant reduction in seizure frequency in patients not on a ketogenic diet, leaving its efficacy for the epilepsy phenotype unproven.

evidence.reference_title: Triheptanoin dramatically reduces paroxysmal motor disorder in patients with GLUT1 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Treatment with triheptanoin resulted in a 90% clinical improvement in non-epileptic paroxysmal manifestations and a normalised brain bioenergetics profile in patients with GLUT1-DS.
